task: Native fp8 MFMA: bitcast OCP e4m3 -> fnuz (tl.float8e4b8) to kill the 161:1 VALU dequant chain
strategy: Pass a_fp8/w1_fp8 to the kernel as .view(torch.uint8) raw bytes; in the k-loop neutralize the single divergent encoding with tl.where(b==0x80,0,b) (OCP -0.0 vs fnuz NaN; 0x7F/0xFF measured absent) then .to(tl.float8e4b8, bitcast=True). Identical 1/4/3 layout with bias 7 vs 8 => each operand reads exactly half, raw tl.dot is exactly 1/4 the true product; folded a single *4.0 into the existing per-128-block a_scale load. Bit-exact. Stacks on the round-1 integrated patch (vectorized graph-captured align + num_stages=1), which is left byte-identical.

notes: THE ROUND-2 WIN IS ENTIRELY THE FP8 DIALECT BITCAST. ISA evidence (AMDGCN dump, case0, before -> after): MFMA opcode v_mfma_f32_16x16x16_f16 x32 -> v_mfma_f32_16x16x32_fp8_fp8 x8 (native 8-bit MFMA, 2x the K per instruction); v_cndmask_b32 1750 -> 0; v_cmp_ne_u16 1728 -> 0; v_lshlrev_b16 192 -> 0; v_add_u16 192 -> 0; v_perm_b32 98 -> 2; arch VGPR 40+136acc=176 -> 104. The entire software fp8->fp16 unpack chain is gone. e2e 4.4478 -> 1.6469 ms geomean (2.70x incremental, 9.14x cumulative vs the frozen baseline), reproduced 3x with 0.2% spread. Bit-exact: cos_diff 4.5e-10..1.3e-9, err_ratio 0.0000 on all 4 cases -- the *4.0 fold is an exact power of two, not an approximation. KEY GENERALIZABLE FACT: torch.float8_e4m3fn (OCP, bias 7) and tl.float8e4b8 (fnuz, bias 8) share the IDENTICAL 1/4/3 bit layout, so a bitcast is an exact halving; Triton on AMD only feeds the 8-bit MFMA from the fnuz types, so ANY gfx942 Triton kernel holding OCP fp8 tensors is silently running a ~161-VALU-per-MFMA software dequant. Correctness needs exactly one guard: OCP 0x80 is -0.0 but fnuz 0x80 is NaN, so tl.where(b==0x80,0,b) on the loaded bytes (0x7F/0xFF are OCP NaN but never occur for finite clamped inputs -- I measured, they are 0). BOTTLENECK HAS SHIFTED AGAIN: the kernel is now MEMORY-bound on weight streaming, not issue-bound. Measured achievable HBM read on this box = 4.35 TB/s; the per-case active-expert weight footprint is 2.59/4.25/5.51/6.29 GB (103/169/219/250 of 256 experts touched), so case0 at 1.00 ms is moving 2.59 GB = 2.6 TB/s = 60% of achievable roofline, and case3 6.29 GB / 2.33 ms = 2.7 TB/s = 62%. Remaining headroom is at most ~1.6x and it is a MEMORY lane, not compute: the whole tile/schedule/AMD-knob space is now re-swept and closed (12 variants, all tie or lose). ROUND-3 STEER: the only large lever left is not fetching the weights at all -- the padded-FLOP waste (7.8% row occupancy at T=16) is now equivalently PADDED-BANDWIDTH waste, since every near-empty BLOCK_M=16 tile still streams its full K=6144 weight column. A DeepGEMM-style compacted block list (or an all-false-token_mask early-exit before the k-loop) would cut both the FLOPs and the HBM traffic together, and at 60% of roofline the bandwidth saving is now the part that pays. ORTHOGONALITY: this patch touches ONLY the k-loop body, the a_scale load, and 4 launcher lines; moe_align_block_size and the graph-cache logic are byte-identical to round 1, so it stacks cleanly.
